01 · Dataset overview

Goal: identify the cohort, exposure and gaps before looking at signal behaviour.

Review at a glance

Source and feature validation passed. The reviewed snapshot is the seed-42, 10-second portfolio-v1 cohort generated with package 0.4.0 and mapped railway geometry. Findings below describe this saved snapshot; refresh them if the configuration or dataset changes.

Fleet-wide inventory Result
Wagons / bogies / axles / wheels 48 / 96 / 192 / 384
Wagons per train / validation / test split 16 / 16 / 16
Scheduled / received / intentionally missing wagon reports 78,954 / 75,277 / 3,677

Signal exploration below uses training data. Validation and test are included only in the inventory and integrity checks. This notebook establishes coverage and reporting behaviour; signal quality and modelling suitability need the next EDA sessions.

1 · Confirm the source

These checks scan both saved datasets. Test is used only for inventory/coverage.

{'portfolio': 'passed', 'features': 'passed'}

Result: portfolio and feature validation both passed. The matching manifests and audit were also reviewed. This confirms the saved-data checks, not model accuracy.

2 · Coverage and unique identities

Open each tab. Counts use complete parent keys, not just inner/outer or left/right.

Coverage finding: each split has 16 distinct wagons: 13 fault variants and 3 healthy controls. All four routes occur in each split, but route counts and duty lengths differ. In training, duties range from 148 to 533 minutes; longer journeys contribute more reports. This deliberately fault-rich cohort does not represent real fleet failure prevalence.

Training route assignments: Avonmouth–Cardiff 4, Cardiff–Swansea 5, London–Avonmouth 4, London–Swansea 3.

Component reporting frequency

Actual received-report counts use full component keys. Train/validation only.

Identity check: the training split contains 16 wagons → 32 bogies → 64 axles → 128 wheels. Its 24,507 received wagon reports correspond to 49,014 bogie, 98,028 axle and 196,056 wheel observations. These are linked levels of the same snapshots, not independent examples. Full parent keys are required.

3 · When did reports disappear?

White cells outside a duty are not outages. Completeness uses expected report slots.

Completeness finding: training contains 4,301 wagon-minute windows: 4,083 complete, 3 partial and 215 silent. Of 25,806 scheduled reports, 24,507 were received (94.97%) and 1,299 are intentionally absent. Blank cells beyond a wagon’s journey are outside its observation horizon, not outages. Silent windows must stay distinct from received reports with unavailable sensors.

4 · Explore one wagon on the map

Markers are sampled; heat layers use all received wagon reports. No wheel duplication.

Map reading: select one wagon to inspect its duty without overlapping other wagons. The line links received positions; a segment spanning an outage is not continuous observed tracking. Aerial/street/topographic layers provide context; clusters show sampled reports and heat layers show reporting density, not fault risk.

The time slider replays received-report density in 30-minute bins. It is not a 10-second position replay or a filter for all map layers. Marker sampling and coordinate rounding in heat layers limit the spatial detail. Python-backed wagon selection needs the running notebook; exported HTML retains its saved selection.

5 · Outage replay

Expected missing slots are synthetic truth, not observations of the controller during silence.

Outage finding: the saved replay confirms 1,299 missing scheduled reports on the three training assets below. Missing-slot positions on the time plot are known synthetic truth, not measurements transmitted while the controller was silent.

Training wagon Assigned scenario Missing reports Silent minutes Partial minutes
FG-WGN-0004 Premature battery depletion 807 134 1
FG-WGN-0021 Persistent controller supply failure 420 70 0
FG-WGN-0039 Bounded controller outage with recovery 72 11 2

The battery case has two distinct gaps, so these three assets produce four outage intervals. Recovery is visible between its gaps; bounded controller reporting also resumes. The persistent controller case remains silent to the journey horizon. No separate communications-network fault is modelled.

6 · Decisions and next session

Decision Evidence / action
Keep this dataset for EDA Source/feature validation passed and audit counts reconcile. No regeneration is needed for this review.
Preserve component identities Use wagon + bogie + axle + wheel keys as appropriate; component rows share parent snapshots.
Account for unequal exposure Routes have 3–5 training wagons each, and duty lengths range from 148–533 minutes. Compare rates with their exposure, not raw counts alone.
Preserve intentional silence Retain expected slots and completeness. Do not replace absent reports with zero-valued measurements.
Keep truth out of predictors Scenario assignments and missing-report truth explain the simulator; they are evaluation evidence, not production observations.
Reserve test data Use training for exploration, validation for checking choices, and test for final evaluation.

Next: 02_healthy_signal_behaviour.ipynb. Start with healthy-control wagons, review all signals at all four levels, and examine operating-state relationships before selecting any model inputs. Dataset consistency is established; model performance and real-world generalisation have not yet been assessed.
